items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: I knew him, naturally, as much as I knew about him. I knew about Chick and both, because I'd been hearing about them for years.

ctx.x: Well after that we had a couple of days, or one day, in the Savoy. Well for years, before -- even before I met Fletcher, or joined him, he and Chick Webb (laughs) had been battling, you know, and music, you know, who's the best, who's greatest, and when the people would pack the place to see it. So while I was with him he's saying we had a -- oh, strenuous rehearsal. He said well I'm going to play against that little guy again. He said this time I must -- I gotta get -- I gotta get him.
I said who? He said Chick Webb. I said all right,

nice, you know. I was for it. I had never played against Chick, and I knew Chick. I knew him, naturally, as much as I knew about him. I knew about Chick and both, because I'd been hearing about them for years. So we get to the Savoy. The place is packed. Ohhh, you never saw so many people. And Fletcher's playing -- you know, Fletcher had something with that beat, dunh dee, dee, pa-daddle doo dee duh duh dum, bah bee, dah dah jussle, and look out and he'd see the people. You'd see the heads bouncing.
